newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung Elec shrs plunge on chip fears.
newsitem.headline: Samsung Elec shrs plunge on chip fears.

text.p: Shares in chipmaker Samsung Electronics Co fell 3,600 won to their daily limit of 56,700 on Friday afternoon on worries the global market for memory chips was worsening, brokers said.
The company is the flagship unit of South Korea's Samsung Group.
Rumours that the spot price for 16-megabit DRAMs had fallen below $10 shook investors, they said. The international spot price fell to $12 a unit in August from $50.10 a year ago.
Unconfirmed reports also circulated on the bourse that Japanese semiconductor makers were selling the chips at $9.3 and that Taiwanese makers were prepared to go as low as $4.

A Citizens Investment Trust Corp fund manager said investors believed Samsung would post a loss this year if the spot price fell below $12. Samsung posted a net profit of 2.51 trillion won in calendar 1995.
Samsung officials refused to comment on the speculation.
A Daewoo Securities broker said selling accelerated on talk that foreign investors were prepared to buy Samsung's stock at around the 56,700 won level.
Samsung shares were actively traded with 187,730 shares changing hands. It ranked sixth in the day's list of most active stocks. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5644
